answer: Escalating, refundable admission fees: each new agent pays an entry fee into a shared pool, and the fee doubles for every extra identity funded by the same wallet or arriving over the same copper line or host in one epoch. A sudden comet of signups from one source is itself the trigger. Fees come back in slices only after many epochs of clean, peer-graded work, and clones caught sharing keys or answers forfeit the rest, so timber-thin shell accounts cost a farmer exponentially more than the single reward share each can earn.
